title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page image is upside down. It is a typed page numbered '- 21 -' from a French typescript on cohomology in topoi, in the style of SGA 4 V. The second side of the sheet was evidently reused: Grothendieck's manuscript notes on cycles on abelian varieties (previous and next pages) are written on the other side, and only faint traces show through, apart from a few hand-added '∀' symbols. The typed mathematics has no connection to the cycle-theory notes.

Content of the typed text:

(1) End of a proof. Setting: a continuous functor u : C → C' between sites, with a condition '(CUC)' guaranteeing suitable covering families. These must be coverings for which Čech cohomology computes things, with fibre products preserved by u.
- Claim: if G is a C'-acyclic sheaf, then its restriction / direct image u_s(G) is C-acyclic.
- 'Acyclic' here means that Čech cohomology Ȟ^q(C~/X, H^0(·)) vanishes for q > 0, where H^0 denotes the underlying presheaf.
- Reduction: it suffices to show H^q(𝒰, H^0(u_s G)) = 0 for the coverings 𝒰 = (U_i → X) provided by (CUC).
- Since u is continuous, u(𝒰) is a covering of u(X).
- By the definition of u_s, the Čech complexes agree: H^q(𝒰, H^0(u_s G)) = H^q(u(𝒰), H^0(G)). This vanishes by C'-acyclicity of G.

(2) Remark. C-acyclicity is not intrinsic: it depends on the site C chosen to present the topos C~, not only on the topos (reference to 3.11).

(3) Start of Proposition 3.4. On a ringed topos (E, A), it begins a list of equivalent intrinsic conditions on an A-Module F. The first is: H^q(S, F) = 0 for all objects S of E and all q > 0. This is the standard characterization of flasque modules (SGA 4 V §4).
errors: The identity of Čech complexes H^q(𝒰, H^0(u_s G)) = H^q(u(𝒰), H^0(G)) needs u to commute with the fibre products U_{i0}×_X…×_X U_{iq}. This is presumably part of hypothesis (CUC) or of the setting, but it is not stated on this page.

'Il suffit de montrer pour toute famille couvrante … dont l'existence est assurée par (CUC)' is a cofinality argument. It is correct provided (CUC) supplies a cofinal system of coverings, which the page leaves implicit.

ideas.what: Under a continuous functor of sites preserving fibre products, Čech-acyclic sheaves on the target restrict to Čech-acyclic sheaves on the source.
ideas.modern_name: Čech acyclicity is preserved by restriction along continuous (morphism-of-sites) functors
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé V (Cohomologie dans les topos), §4

ideas.what: Acyclicity with respect to a site is not a topos-invariant notion; it is replaced by an intrinsic one, H^q(S, F) = 0 for all S and q > 0.
ideas.modern_name: Flasque sheaves/modules in a ringed topos
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 V, Définition 4.1 and following propositions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a sheet of reused typescript paper containing standard SGA 4 V material on Čech acyclicity and flasque modules in topoi. It is unrelated to the handwritten cycle-theory notes in this folder and contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; it is the typed side of a sheet reused for manuscript notes.
The '{+∀+}' insertions are handwritten '∀' symbols added to the typescript next to 'q > 0'.
The handwritten '87' in the corner is the archive page number; the typed page number is '- 21 -'.
'H^0' in the formulas is the script ℋ^0 (underlying presheaf functor), not ordinary H^0.
'C'-acyclique' is the typescript's 'C′-acyclique' (acyclic for the site C′).
